continuous_integration.artifact_source_delta: The exact source passed Rust formatting, Clippy, tests, examples, documentation, contract jobs, Apple identity, Fascia, CompanionKit, Companion, native Mac, and Simulator CI surfaces. Candidate CLI smoke failed only because a second workflow grep still expected the 1.2.0 banner after the protocol assertion had been updated to 1.2.1. Post-source workflow-only commit c0ea1ba corrected that assertion; its Rust, Apple, and contract jobs passed before a separate static-surface step failed. Neither run is represented as fully green. The exact clean source separately passed the universal native build, bundle verification, Apple signing/notarization, mounted Gatekeeper assessment, immutable origin round trip, production website-to-DMG digest round trip, and an installed-app startup with a healthy 1.2.1 factory.

dark_deployment.post_source_changes: Production first disabled the rejected RC10 download, then pinned the exact immutable RC11 URL and SHA-256 after notarization and origin verification. Later website source adds the RC11 version and build number required by the fail-closed native update banner without changing those bytes. The root serves the canonical Ship/Fork/Claim timeline, signed catalog media is publicly projectable, and Registry and Claims relayers remain funded and narrowly enabled for the owner-attended Ship and friend Claim window.

rejected_release_candidates.reason: The Mac bundle omitted share/apple-identity, so Companion dependency resolution failed before iPhone signing and the UI collapsed the failure into an unactionable Apple Account message.

Owner-attended first-open acceptance found that the app entered device setup without first welcoming the person, explaining the intention-to-native-iPhone-app relationship, or giving enough plain-language purpose for each prerequisite.

Owner-attended Registry acceptance found that the Mac app rejected valid local Registry responses and exposed neither CLI activation nor the init, deploy, Companion-approval, and recipient-signing path, leaving the person unable to begin the end-to-end Ship walkthrough.

Owner-attended init acceptance found that the CLI abandoned its local adoption request after ten seconds while Xcode correctly continued the real Simulator build, falsely reporting a connection error and hiding all subsequent progress.

Owner-attended deploy acceptance found that the publication scanner treated the short byte prefix ghp_ inside compressed PNG data as a complete credential and rejected safe source before Companion approval.
RC6 predates deploy-time signed app slugs, authenticated global-alias review, the exact friend handoff page, and the private intended-phone selector required for this real Ship-to-friend mission.

The owner-attended Ship exposed two live client blockers: the Mac compared the constructor-patched Registry runtime against the template hash instead of the threshold-signed activation, and whole-response source downloads were unreliable at real app size. The live Builder-authorized Ship was reconciled after focused fixes, but RC7 is not the friend-install candidate.
RC8 predates signed public app icons and screenshots, the canonical Ship/Fork/Claim website timeline, and the exact Claim handoff implemented for the current real-user path.

Owner-attended first-open use exposed two blockers: launchd bootstrap succeeded but a redundant kickstart raced RunAtLoad and was falsely reported as a service-start failure, and the Mac client could not decode the factory's valid pairing_uri response into pairingURI.

release_candidate_evidence.focused_release_verification: macOS 41 tests, Companion 41 tests, Companion warnings-as-errors build, focused service-install Rust tests and Clippy, Rust formatting, a clean universal native build, signed and notarized native bundle verification, mounted Gatekeeper acceptance, immutable GitHub-origin and tohseno.com download digest round trips, and installed-app startup with a healthy 1.2.1 factory passed; the Connect Companion button and physical iPhone were not exercised

blocking_reason: RC11 is built from exact clean commit 82aa020, Developer ID signed, Apple-notarized under submission e9cdaddc-6d88-462f-bdc5-11d90a501186, stapled, mounted, Gatekeeper-accepted, published as an immutable GitHub prerelease, origin/public-download verified, and activated on tohseno.com's release-candidate channel with digest bac1ea3222c1ebbad82ced592ba33ef465eba2995f6413acd14edd5d8c8c5c35. RC10 was disabled and rejected after owner-observed launchd and pairing-response failures. The installed RC11 app exercised the real startup path and reached a healthy 1.2.1 factory, but the Connect Companion button and physical iPhone path were not exercised and are not claimed. The exact-source CI run passed product, Rust, Apple, and contract jobs but retained one stale workflow assertion failure; a later workflow-only fix passed those jobs before an unrelated static-surface step failed, so no full CI success is claimed. The remaining external steps are the Companion pairing ritual, a second human's exact-release Claim, local build with their Apple identity, and install on their intended iPhone; no clean-Mac, Workshop Session, or remaining physical fact is claimed yet.
